title: Tenant Sentinel Profiles for Embedding Model Swap Runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable, tenant-centric runbook ("Tenant Sentinel Profiles") that governs embedding model swaps (new model onboarding and deprecation) with automated probes for semantic drift, latency regressions, cost exposure, and index compatibility. The runbook should produce a per-tenant safety profile used to decide traffic slices for dark-launch, canary, gradual rollout, and hard deprecation windows.

Why: Existing onboarding patterns rely on coarse global signals and manual checks. We need a lightweight, automated way to reason about risk per tenant (index size, query distribution, tail latency, SLA sensitivity) so we can deploy higher-quality embedding models without causing regressions or cost surprises.

Scope:
- Define the Tenant Sentinel Profile schema (static + telemetry-driven attributes) used by routing and rollout services. Schema fields include: index_encoding_format, median_query_length, 95th_percentile_tokens, avg_cosine_shift (semantic probe), latency_p50/p95, recent-failure-rate, cost-velocity, and fallback_compatibility_score.
- Implement a live prober that runs semantic alignment checks using a tenant-specific probe-set (seed queries + golden answers) and reports KL-like divergence metrics and recall loss.
- Integrate sentinel profiles into the embed-routing layer so that: (a) dark-launch traffic is only routed to tenants with low-risk profiles; (b) canary weight calculations are tenant-aware; (c) automatic hold/backoff triggers exist for per-tenant rollouts.
- Add cost-guardrails that throttle model selection for high-cost tenants (e.g., heavy sequence lengths) and provide suggestions (quantized variant vs full-precision) in the rollout plan.
- Provide operator runbook docs, alerting thresholds, and rollback triggers.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Schema stored in metadata service and accessible to routing policies.
2) Probe job that can execute per-tenant semantic checks and produces a numeric alignment delta metric.
3) Routing respects profile-derived policies for dark-launch and canary (verified in staging with synthetic tenants).
4) Produces rollout audit log entries (PR link, dataset snapshot, probe results, decision) for each swap.
5) Operator docs + a one-click abort on console for any tenant with alignment delta > threshold or latency increase > 25% p95.

Non-goals: index migration tooling (out of scope), model training, or building new embedding models. This is about safety, telemetry, routing, and processes.
